chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Isma'il told me, saying: Abul Abbas ibn Muni'a told us, saying: Sheiban ibn Furukh told us, saying: Davud ibn Abi al-Furat told us, saying: Al-Ba' ibn Ahmar told us, saying: Akrama told us, from Ibn Abbas, saying:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) drew four lines on the ground and said: 'Do you know what this is?' We said: 'God and His Messenger know best.' Then the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The four best women of the people of Paradise are: Khadijah bint Khuwaylid, Fatimah bint Muhammad, Mary bint Imran, and Asiya bint Muzahim, the wife of Pharaoh.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the four best women in Paradise according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Al-Khisal*, this hadith employs the rhetorical device of drawing four lines to emphasize the supreme status of Khadijah, Fatimah, Mary, and Asiya as the pinnacle of female virtue. Shia scholars often interpret this grouping as representing the four archetypes of piety: the devoted wife, the prophetic daughter, the chaste worshiper, and the royal convert, thereby establishing a comprehensive model for female spiritual excellence.
